narrative.overview:
The workspace is a sheet of neutral glass: near-black (or near-white) grounds in three quiet tonal steps, hairline dividers, and system type. Lagoon Teal is the ink. It marks what is linked, selected, focused or active: wiki links and tags, the active ribbon icon, the focused tab's underline, the keyboard row in the file tree, the text caret, and the active node in the graph. Teal ink on glass is the whole identity. Everything else stays out of the way so the note can lead.

The layout is the familiar vault workspace: a ribbon, a file tree, tabbed and splittable editor panes, and a right sidebar for graph, backlinks, outline and tags. It is drawn as a native Mac app, not a copy of Obsidian. The chrome is dense and precise: 44pt title bar, 24pt status bar, 13pt UI text. The writing surface is generous: 16pt body in a centred column of up to 780pt, 56pt side insets, and 96pt of run-out below the last line.

Controls are quiet until touched. They sit flush with the chrome, without borders or boxes, and show themselves only through a rounded tint on hover, selection or focus. They follow macOS conventions: system controls, menus, sheets and keyboard shortcuts. The app must never read as a web page in a window.
keyCharacteristics: One ink: Lagoon Teal is the only brand colour. Other hues are functional (drop target, callouts, graph, syntax).
Flat, tonal depth: three grounds and 1pt dividers. Material and shadow only on floating, transient surfaces.
SF Pro throughout, with SF Mono for code. No brand typeface.
Light and Dark are equal citizens, built from paired tokens.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Lagoon Teal is the only colour that means "this is yours, active, or linked". Functional hues signal a specific job (drop here, warning, linked node) and never decorate.

rules.name: The Tint, Don't Fill Rule
rules.body: Teal shows up as a translucent tint behind a control (18–30%) or a 2pt bar. It is never a solid teal slab behind chrome. The exception is the prominent button, which uses the system's own tinted style.

rules.name: The System Voice Rule
rules.body: Use SF Pro and SF Mono through the system font APIs. No bundled or brand typefaces. Hierarchy is size and weight, never a second family.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces never cast shadows. Shadow and material belong to floating, transient surfaces (palettes, toasts, drag previews) and to state (the split glow).

dos: Do take every colour, size and inset from `VGTheme`. Add new tokens there, with a dark and a light value, rather than writing `Color(red:…)` or `NSColor(red:…)` literals in a view.
Do use Lagoon Teal as a tint (18–30%) or a 2pt bar to mark active, selected, focused or linked. Use Lagoon Teal Bright when teal is the text or glyph colour.
Do use system controls (`.borderedProminent`, segmented pickers, toggles, sheets, confirmation dialogs, native search fields) and SF Symbols, sized to the 13pt UI and 15pt icon scale.
Do keep depth tonal: ribbon, then chrome, then editor ground, with 1pt dividers.
Do keep prose in the centred column of up to 780pt, at 16pt with +3pt leading.
Do design every surface in both Light and Dark.
donts: Don't make the app look like a web app in a window: no custom web-style buttons, CSS-like cards, hover-only affordances without keyboard equivalents, or reinvented system controls.
Don't clone Obsidian's look. Keep the familiar vault layout, but not its purple identity or its exact chrome. The ink is Lagoon Teal.
Don't put shadows on resting surfaces (Flat-at-Rest Rule). Shadow and material are for palettes, toasts, drag previews and the split glow.
Don't use Drop Target Blue or the callout hues for anything other than their job.
Don't introduce a second type family. Hierarchy is SF Pro size and weight.
